subject: Bug when assigning a new scalar to an existing scalar

messages.author: 243d9dde5595d8e7
messages.subject: Bug when assigning a new scalar to an existing scalar
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to figure out why Nimble allows(compiles)  this: 


test1 <- nimbleFunction ( run = function (indx = double(1) ) {
    if(  length(indx)==2 & indx[1]==indx[2] ) {
        aa <- indx[1] 
    } else {
        newindx <- indx
        aa         <- length(newindx)
    }
    output <- 1 + aa
    returnType(double(0))
    return(output)
})

 but doesn't compile this :

test2 <- nimbleFunction(run = function(indx = double(1)) {
    if(  length(indx)==2 & indx[1]==indx[2] ) {
        newindx <- indx[1]
        aa          <- newindx     ## THIS IS THE MAIN CHANGE IN THIS FUNCTION
    } else {
        newindx <- indx
        aa          <- length(newindx)
    }
    output <- 1 + aa
    returnType(double(0))
    return(output)
})
 
in which case  the error message is :

> c_test2 <- compileNimble(test2)
Warning, mismatched dimensions in assignment: newindx <- ARG1_indx_. Going to browser(). Press Q to exitFALSE
Called from: sizeAssignAfterRecursing(code, symTab, typeEnv)
Browse[1]> debug: if (assignmentTypeWarn(LHS$type, RHStype)) {
    message(paste0("Warning, RHS numeric type is losing information in assignment to LHS.", 
        nimDeparse(code)))
}
Browse[2]> 


In both cases, the uncompiled version test1 and test2 work correctly.


Thank you !!


Soledad

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Bug when assigning a new scalar to an existing scalar
parts:
In the second example, you are first using newindx as a scalar and then attempting to use it as a vector.  It can’t change types.  If it is created as a scalar the first time it is used, you can keep using it only as a scalar.

As with most issues, we need to generate more friendly error messages.

Perry

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Bug when assigning a new scalar to an existing scalar
parts:
A little more detail, the problem is that the newindx variable is being assigned as both a scalar and as a vector, in two different places, which is causing a problem for the compiler.

First, note that indx is defined to be a vector (a 1-dimensional object) because of the specification:

The first assignment into newindx defines newindx to be a scalar (0-dimensional object):
newindx <- indx[1]   ## indexing as indx[1] assigns a *scalar* into newindx

The second assignment into newindx defines it to be a vector (1-dimensional object):
newindx <- indx   ## indx is a vector, hence this assigns a *vector* into newindx

Clearing up that discrepancy should fix it.
